CONTEXT DUMP — T572 (load-test lanes must never touch the live kanban store). RED/GREEN evidence, design decisions, denominators.

== (1) THE INCIDENT AND ROOT CAUSE (from T567's reconstruction; re-verified here) ==

The T559 load test (2026-08-21) dispatched six dummy lanes via `tools/runner --max-wall 600 --task-id TL1x -- python3 -c 'import time; time.sleep(300)'` (untracked/bakeoff/t559-drive.sh). The runner AUTO-CLAIMS the named row at launch (WORKER-CHANNEL, tools/runner ~line 1428): `managent claim <task-id> --agent <model>`. The host guard SIGKILLed each lane (exit 124). The runner's auto-done fires only on exit 0, so a guard-killed lane leaves the row `in_progress` — claimed, never closed. Six rows TL1A..TL1F sat in_progress in docs/infra/managent/tasks.json until T567 retired them. T567's reconstruction: there was no resurrection — the 'close' in commit e341eb1's message never landed in the store. Also verified here: the T427 live-store fixture guard (ids containing DOCTOR/FIXTURE/SEED/PROBE/ARM/TEST) would NOT have tripped — 'TL1A' carries no marker. MANAGENT_TEST=1 was not set. So the live store had no defense against this injection shape.

== (2) THE FIX (job 1) — harness points at a scratch MANAGENT_STORE ==

untracked/bakeoff/t559-drive.sh now: seeds TL1A..TL1F into $RUN/store/tasks.json (a scratch store under untracked/bakeoff/t559/store) via `managent add --note 'T559 load-test dummy lane'`; exports MANAGENT_STORE=$RUN/store/tasks.json for the whole drive, so the runner's auto-claim AND auto-done inherit it (the child managent resolves state_path from the env var — src/managent/main.zig:382); runs the lanes exactly as before (host guard ON, WEIZIGO_HOST_MEM_AVAIL_MB=100 injection); at the end asserts the LIVE store holds zero TL1* rows and retires the six lanes from the scratch store. The runner itself is untouched (cull/reap logic out of scope). Run records still land in $ROOT/untracked/runs/TL1x.json (repo_root = $ROOT) — that is evidence by design, not pollution. Verified the mechanics standalone (seed → one guard-kill lane → live store zero TL1* → retire) with lane exit 124 and the scratch row in_progress; `zsh -n` passes.

== (3) THE REGRESSION ARM (job 2) — tools/regression-managent-store-pollution.sh, wired into zig build test ==

Scratch repo under /tmp/weizigo/t572-store-pollution-*; the REAL live store is read-only (SHA-256 snapshotted before, asserted byte-identical after). Binary resolution MANAGENT_BIN → zig-out/bin/managent → bin/managent; SKIP when none (the runner's auto-claim needs it). The pollution checker (the arm): scans a tasks.json for a row whose id matches ^TL<digit>* (the TL1x convention) or whose note/bundle names a load test / dummy lane; RED (exit 1) when any found, GREEN (exit 0) otherwise. Arms:
  A. the fix (known-good): guard-kill lane (WEIZIGO_HOST_MEM_AVAIL_MB=100, `sleep 120` child — the T559 lane shape) with MANAGENT_STORE=scratch → claim lands in the scratch store (TL2A in_progress there), live-store stand-in never created.
  B. seeded defect (known-bad → known-good): the PRE-FIX shape — same lane WITHOUT MANAGENT_STORE → dummy row TL2C left in_progress in the stand-in store (the T559 leak reproduced) → checker RED; `managent retire TL2C` (the exact T567 scrub verb) → checker GREEN.
  C. clean-exit path: a lane that exits 0 runs auto-done against the scratch store; for a <10s lane the T390 claim-window refusal ('REJECTED: TL2B was claimed 1s before this done') proves the done ATTEMPT was redirected; stand-in stays absent.
  D. null control: an empty store is GREEN (specificity, no false positive).
  E. real live store: byte-identical throughout; checker GREEN on it.

One script bug caught during development (test-first working): the first version did not `export MANAGENT_STORE` for the runner invocations in arms A/C (only for the seed adds), so the runner's child claim hit the stand-in store and 'task TL2A not found' — the suite went red on arm A and the stand-in got created by the failed claim's migration write. Fix: seed_lane now registers into the SAME ambient env the runner's child sees (exported for the fix arms, unset for the seeded-defect arm). The failing run's readings are what made the env-propagation contract visible.

== (4) DESIGN DECISIONS ==

- Scratch store, not cleanup-on-every-exit-path. The brief preferred the scratch store (regression-dispatch-verification.sh:82 pattern); a SIGKILL has no exit path at all, so 'cleanup on every exit path' cannot be made airtight — the scratch store makes cleanup moot. The runner's auto-claim is by design for real worker rows; the bug was a LOAD TEST reusing real task ids against the live store.
- Checker markers: id ^TL<digit>* OR note/bundle text 'load-test'/'dummy lane'. Retired rows live in archive.json, so a tasks.json scan sees only live rows — a retire is a true cleanup, matching how T567 scrubbed. TL<digit> ids exist nowhere in the live store (verified: 0/254 rows match) and are the project's test-lane convention, so the pattern is safe from false positives.
- The regression exercises the RUNNER PATH, not the untracked harness file. The harness (untracked/bakeoff/t559-drive.sh) is host-durable only and dies on a fresh clone; a committed regression cannot grep it (claimlint C2 would flag the missing path). The durable substrate is the runner's auto-claim path, which is exactly what arm A/C exercise — any future load-test harness that follows the scratch-store pattern is safe, and the composition is pinned by the suite.
- No runner changes (out of scope per brief): the auto-claim/done logic, cull and reap are untouched; only the store-pollution path (the harness env) was changed.
